name: Livid Violet
lede: Livid Violet is a dark, greyed purple recorded by Ridgway in 1912 and classed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 as a light grayish red.

sections.title: A dark, bruised purple
sections.body:
Our data files this under the violet family rather than from a pigment or a place [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots it on plate XXXVII at hue 61″, tone i, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same area as block 18, "light grayish red" [1]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 separately gives it a first record of 1905 [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 44, chroma 20, hue 328 degrees: dark and low in saturation [1].

Its nearest computed neighbors are [[dusky-mauve|Dusky Mauve]] and [[livid-purple|Livid Purple]], both 3.1 units off and redder, and [[deep-hyssop-violet|Deep Hyssop Violet]], 3.7 units off and purpler [2]. The closest everyday name is [[plum]], about 10.9 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 19, as photographed (11 by the stricter within-painting measure), which makes it rarer than 67 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 4.0 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive, though on a small base of 6 paintings [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 36 percent of its matches, by lightness rank within the canvas; varnish cannot fake that ranking [4]. The earliest match is a 1490 painting by Bartolomeo Vivarini, 422 years before the name's first record in 1912; that only shows the hue existed long before anyone wrote it down, not that any pigment did, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4].
